cards.front: What is an enum in Java?
cards.back: A type with a fixed set of constants, declared with the enum keyword
cards.extra: Each constant is a singleton instance of the enum class. You cannot create more instances at runtime.

cards.front: What class does every enum implicitly extend?
cards.back: java.lang.Enum
cards.extra: Which is why an enum cannot extend another class — that slot is taken. It can still implement interfaces.

cards.front: What is EnumSet for?
cards.back: A set of elements of a single enum type, stored as a bit vector
cards.extra: Very compact and fast, and it iterates in declaration order. It rejects null elements.

cards.front: What is the difference between an exception and an error condition here?
cards.back: An exception is an unexpected event at run time that disrupts normal instruction flow
cards.extra: Unhandled, it terminates the program and prints a stack trace starting from the throw site.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::01 Exception Handling

cards.front: What does the File class represent?
cards.back: A path to a file or directory, plus operations on it — exists, delete, mkdir, list
cards.extra: It is metadata only: File does not read or write contents. Streams and readers do that.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: Which classes read bytes from a file, and which read characters?
cards.back: FileInputStream/FileOutputStream handle bytes; FileReader/FileWriter handle characters
cards.extra: Pick by content: images and archives on the byte side, text on the char side with an explicit charset.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: What does final mean on a variable, a method and a class?
cards.back: Variable: cannot be reassigned. Method: cannot be overridden. Class: cannot be subclassed
cards.extra: For a reference variable it fixes the reference, not the object's contents.

cards.front: What is inheritance?
cards.back: Creating a new class from an existing one so it reuses fields and methods, and can add its own
cards.extra: The subclass gets the superclass's accessible members; extends declares the relationship.

cards.front: What is InputStream?
cards.back: The abstract superclass of all byte input streams
cards.extra: It defines read() and is not useful by itself — you use a concrete subclass such as FileInputStream.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: What does instanceof return?
cards.back: true if the object is an instance of the given class or interface, else false
cards.extra: It is a runtime check; false for null rather than an exception. Since Java 16 it can also declare a pattern variable.

cards.front: What is an interface, in this course's words?
cards.back: A fully abstract class: a group of abstract methods with no bodies
cards.extra: A class implements it with implements and must provide those methods. Since Java 8 it may also hold default and static methods.

cards.front: What is the difference between an input stream and an output stream?
cards.back: An input stream reads from a source; an output stream writes to a destination
cards.extra: The direction is from the program's point of view, not the file's.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: What methods does Iterator define?
cards.back: hasNext(), next(), and remove()
cards.extra: Every collection returns one from iterator(). Removing through the iterator is the safe way to delete while looping.

cards.front: What is a keyword in Java?
cards.back: A reserved word with a special meaning to the compiler, which cannot be used as an identifier
cards.extra: int, class, new. Using one as a variable name is a compile error, not a warning.

cards.front: What is the shape of a lambda expression?
cards.back: (parameters) -> body
cards.extra: The body is an expression or a block. The lambda's type is inferred from the target functional interface.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::03 Lambda Expressions

cards.front: What is the difference between LinkedBlockingQueue and ArrayBlockingQueue?
cards.back: Linked is node-based and optionally bounded; array is fixed-capacity
cards.extra: An unbounded linked queue can grow until memory runs out, which hides a slow-consumer problem.

cards.front: What does LinkedHashSet guarantee?
cards.back: Insertion order when iterating, unlike a plain HashSet
cards.extra: It costs a little memory for the linked list that maintains the order.

cards.front: What is LinkedList?
cards.back: A doubly linked list implementing both List and Deque
cards.extra: Fast at the ends, slow for index access — it must walk the nodes.

cards.front: What does the List interface guarantee?
cards.back: An ordered collection with index access that allows duplicates
cards.extra: Unlike Set, position matters and the same element may appear twice.

cards.front: What does the Map interface store?
cards.back: Key/value pairs, with unique keys mapping to values
cards.extra: It is not a Collection: no iterator over elements, and it has its own hierarchy.

cards.front: What is a method?
cards.back: A block of code that performs a specific task, callable by name
cards.extra: It keeps a program from being one long main: one task per method, reused and tested separately.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::02 Attributes and Methods

cards.front: What is a multidimensional array?
cards.back: An array of arrays — each element is itself an array
cards.extra: int[][] grid = new int[3][4];. Rows can have different lengths, since each is a separate array.

cards.front: What is multi-catch, and which version added it?
cards.back: catch (IOException | SQLException e) — Java 7
cards.extra: It removes duplicated handling blocks. The caught variable is implicitly final.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::01 Exception Handling

cards.front: What is the built-in Java logging framework, and its package?
cards.back: java.util.logging (JUL)
cards.extra: Available without any dependency; SLF4J with Logback or Log4j2 is more common in applications.
